paragraphs: Rav Avya the elder and his son Rava. (See there: the error, for he did not have a son Rava.) He did not attend Rav Yosef’s lecture in Pumbedita, who sent Rav Dimi bar Yosef to conceal him; Rav Avya said he had not come because he was ill, chapter Tefillat Hashachar. This is not there or in the Jerusalem Talmud; it is an error. It should read: Rabbi Avya was ill and did not attend Rav Yosef’s lecture. Next day Abaye wished to appease Rav Yosef and asked him, “Why did the master not come?” He answered, “My heart was weak,” Tefillat Hashachar 28, beginning of b. Rav Avya came to Rava’s house, his feet soiled with mud. He put him on a bed; Rava was upset and sought to distress him with questions, which he answered. Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said, “Blessed is the Merciful One who did not shame him,” Shabbat 46a. He asked Rav Huna, who told him, “A raven has flown,” Beitzah 21a. He asked Rabbah bar Rav Huna, who likewise said, “A raven has flown,” Chullin 124b. See there: he was of Pumbedita (see under resh, Rava bar Rav Avya, at length, and Yuchasin’s error). Rabbah bar bar Chana, Kiddushin 39a. Rabbah bar Rav Huna found Rabbah bar bar Chana, come to Babylonia, eating from the fat over the stomach. They told Abaye, Pesachim 51a; the reading is Rav Avya the elder (see there). In Rav Yosef’s name, chapter Mefannin; Beitzah 13, end of b. He said in Rabbi Ammi’s name, Chullin 50a. Rav Avya married Rami bar Pappa’s sister, Bava Batra 100b. When she died, he held a standing-and-sitting ceremony. Rav Yosef said he erred in two things; Abaye and Rava each added another error. There the name is unqualified Rav Avya, without “elder.” Since Yuchasin lists it under Rav Avya the elder, I retained his arrangement and wrote my observations. Af Al Pi 56, end of b: Rami bar Chama’s sister was married to Rav Avya; her marriage contract was lost. They came before Rav Yosef, who said, etc.; Abaye said, etc. Here too it says Rav Avya without qualification. (Bava Batra has Rami bar Pappa’s sister, Ketubbot Rami bar Chama’s. It appears both concern one marriage, since both mention Rav Yosef and Abaye; one of Pappa/Chama is an error.) Rav Pappa took Rav Avya the elder along and expounded, Mo'ed Katan 24b. His hand came out of joint while he was sitting before Rav Yosef, end of Chavit. Rav Avya, Shabbat 22, end of a, and 23: Rav Avya said, etc.; Rav Nechemyah said; Abaye told him, etc.; Rav Yosef told him, Shabbat 63a, 109b. Rav Avya said, etc. Menachot 33: Rav Avya said avakta, “loop”; this is the Arukh’s reading, while ours has Rav Adda. Rabbah bar Chanan. There, 37b: Rav Avya bar Rav Avya should read Rav Acha bar Rav Avya (see there). Rav Mordekhai told Rav Ashi: Rav Avya objects.
